title: When the Postcard Falls
premise: Astrid Sandoval ghostwrites the memoir of celebrated novelist Elias Vane, her ex-mentor and the man whose betrayal ended her career, when a postcard lost in the mail for eleven years arrives — a letter she wrote him the night he abandoned her. As she drafts his life story in his voice, the letter's resurfacing forces both of them to relive the choice that destroyed them: he took credit for her manuscript to save his dying wife's treatment, trading Astrid's future for loyalty to someone else. When the truth threatens to surface in the finished memoir, Astrid must decide whether to expose him or let the past stay buried, and Elias must finally let her go — or ask her to stay after the last train leaves. She stays, but on her own terms: her name on the next book, her past reclaimed, belonging chosen rather than earned.
about_author: Mirabel Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's unsent letters before writing her own stories. She lives in a coastal town where the last train of the evening still runs, and she swears she's never missed it — yet.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She begins ghostwriting Elias Vane's memoir, hiding her identity behind a contract and a decade of practiced invisibility. The emotional beat is controlled resentment: she tells herself this is just work, but every chapter she writes in his voice costs her something she can't name.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A water-stained postcard arrives at Elias's house — her own letter from the night he betrayed her, delayed over a decade by a dead letter office. Elias reads it before she can stop him, and the room fills with everything neither of them ever said. The beat is shock cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Flashbacks braid with the present: young Astrid delivering her finished manuscript, Elias accepting it, the hospital corridor where his wife's treatment depended on a bestseller. The beat is devastating context — the reader learns why he did it before Astrid fully does.

chapters.title: The Interview
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He insists on recording sessions to 'get the memoir right,' using them to confess in fragments he hopes she'll forgive. Astrid transcribes his justifications and hears, for the first time, the price he paid too. The beat is uneasy empathy complicating her anger.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Debt
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. His late wife's sister arrives to help with the memoir and begins asking pointed questions about the first novel's true authorship. Elias realizes the truth is leaking, and that protecting Astrid now means contradicting the legend he built. The beat is dread of exposure.

chapters.title: Drafts and Confessions
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She rewrites the memoir's pivotal chapter to tell the truth in his voice, then deletes it — twice. A near-kiss in the archive room after a storm leaves them both shaken. The beat is longing she refuses to name, loyalty to her own wound versus the pull toward him.

chapters.title: The Sister's Evidence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The sister-in-law finds the original manuscript pages in Elias's attic, dated in Astrid's hand, and threatens to go public. Elias offers her the estate's letters in exchange for silence; Astrid discovers the bargain and feels betrayed by his protection all over again. The beat is the past tightening its grip.

chapters.title: Last Train
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Contract finished, she packs to leave before dawn, believing second chances are for people with better timing. Elias asks her to stay — not to finish the book, but to stay — and she refuses, because staying feels like forgiving too cheaply. The beat is heartbreak as self-protection.

chapters.title: The Chapter in Her Voice
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At the memoir's launch event, he abandons the prepared reading and publicly credits Astrid Sandoval as the author of the novel that made him, surrendering the legend to save the truth. The beat is the climax: sacrifice as the only apology that means anything.

chapters.title: When the Postcard Falls
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Weeks later, her byline on a new book of her own, she finds Elias waiting at the small station with her postcard, finally returned to her. She lets the last train leave without her — this time by choice. The beat is belonging chosen freely, survival no longer at anyone else's price.
